newsitem.title: CHINA: Hong Kong police round up Vietnamese migrants.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong police round up Vietnamese migrants.

text.p: Hong Kong police have arrested 18 suspected illegal immigrants from Vietnam after a dragnet by land, sea and air prompted by claims that hundreds had jumped off a ship in the territory, police said on Tuesday.

Police said they captured the 18 boatpeople on Lantau Island. Those detained told police they had been dropped off by a freighter on Sunday night off Lantau, the territory's largest island, and had claimed that 600 illegal immigrants were on board.
However, a police spokeswoman said police had called off the large-scale search late on Monday and were now probing whether the detainees had hoaxed them.
The latest batch of so-called "boatpeople" left Quang Ninh in northern Vietnam 12 days ago, Hong Kong television said.
In recent years, Hong Kong has been repatriating tens of thousands of illegal Vietnamese migrants who were not recognised as genuine refugees.
Repatriation became more frequent in the months approaching Hong Kong's return to Chinese rule on July 1. Beijing demanded all detention camps be cleared by the time of the handover.
But some 3,000 Vietnamese are still in the territory, the remnants of a human floodtide who left Vietnam after the communists won the war there in 1975.
